title: Stratified workload batcher gardener — continuous profiling and safe apply
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a stratified batching recommendation engine (the 'gardener') that continuously profiles active workloads, synthesizes per-cohort batching and caching heuristics, and performs guarded configuration rollouts. The gardener should: 1) ingest lightweight request traces from runtime (sequence length, model, route, KV cache hit/miss, latency, tokens), 2) produce tiered batch/caching profiles per workload cohort, 3) score candidate profiles by estimated cost delta and latency SLO risk, and 4) apply changes via a controlled rollout with shadow evaluation, canary, and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Profiler produces cohort signatures and baseline profiles covering >= 95% of traffic for targeted routes; 2) Recommendation engine outputs candidate profiles with estimated token-cost and 99th-percentile latency prediction; 3) Shadow-apply runs produce telemetry that matches production within 5% for key metrics; 4) Canary rollout mechanism can auto-rollback within 10 minutes if thresholds exceeded; 5) End-to-end e2e test demonstrating safe apply/rollback on a synthetic workload (cost reduction >= 8% without SLO violation).
design_notes: Key design decisions and heuristics: - Stratification: group by (route, model_family, median_seq_len_bucket, customer_tier, live_qps_bucket) to balance specificity vs sample size. - Heuristic rules: favour increasing batch_size for stable low-variance cohorts; reduce batch_size for cohorts with high 99p latency spikes. - KV-aware profiles: when KV hit-rate > 60%, prefer longer micro-batches and aggressive prefix caching TTL extension. - Interaction with autoscaling: ensure recommended batching respects min-max concurrency and does not cause excessive GPU queueing. - Risk scoring: combine delta_cost_score, latency_risk_score, and sample_confidence to compute priority. - Safety guardrails: no single-customer profile change without manual review; global low-latency tiers (SLA customers) default to conservative profiles.
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow apply candidates for 48h on production traffic (no affect); 2) Run offline validation comparing shadow vs real path (latency, tail, and model output diffs); 3) Canary apply to 1% traffic for 1h; 4) Linear phased expansion (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with automated hold/rollback gates; 5) Full apply to cohort. Gate conditions: tail latency + error rate + model output divergence + cost delta thresholds. Manual abort path: operations UI with freeze and immediate rollback button.
telemetry_metrics: List of metrics to capture: runtime.tokens_per_request, runtime.avg_latency_ms, runtime.99p_latency_ms, runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate, runtime.batch_size_applied, runtime.queue_time_ms, cost.estimated_per_token, cost.estimated_delta_pct, correctness.model_output_divergence_score
rollback_strategy: Automated rollback if any gating metric exceeds thresholds: 99p latency increases > 12% AND absolute delta > 50ms OR error rate increase > 0.1%. After rollback, flag cohort for human review and mark profile as rejected. Rollbacks must create tracelog and attach last 72h shard traces for debugging. Keep previous profile in versioned store for immediate reapply if needed.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for signature matching and scoring functions. 2) Integration test with synthetic trace generator that simulates bursts and KV-hit variations. 3) Staging deployment with recorded production traffic replay for end-to-end validation. 4) Chaos tests injecting slow kernels and partial GPU OOM to validate safe fallback and rollback. 5) Post-release canary dashboard to monitor real-time deviations.
implementation_notes: - Extend lightweight profiler proto: add median_seq_len, kv_hit_estimate, route_hash. - New service 'gardener' implemented as stateless recommender + persistent profile store (versioned). - Use existing rollout controller with new gates; add shadow exporter to collect pairwise telemetry. - Prefer incremental apply via feature flags and route-level overrides. - Add throttling to prevent more than N profile changes per cluster per hour.
open_questions: 1) How to best handle model-variant fallbacks when batched latency causes model divergence? 2) Should we auto-throttle recommendations during predictable diurnal peaks? 3) Decide TTL policy for cohort signatures to avoid staleness vs noisy churn.
